bearing but she insists on working part-time and has been on her 
feet over the last few weeks. Yesterday she ran a few errands 
and then started noticing increasing R heel pain. She always has 
some R ankle swelling and felt that the swelling was slightly 
worse. She denies fevers, chills, redness or warmth in the R 
heel region. She called her podiatrist and was initially told to 
take ibuprofen and have some bedrest but the pain kept getting 
worse and she decided to come in to ED. She had plain films in 
ED which were neg for fractures/acute abn. She was noted to have 
low grade temp of 100.1 and was admitted. She was also mildly 
dehydrated and given fluids
   Pt denies any symptoms concerning for infection such as 
sorethroat, cough, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, 
dysuria, frquency, urgency.  She also denies melena, 
hematochezia or hematuria. She feels much better now. Her pain 
is relieved by percocet

Brief Hospital Course:
AP: ___ yo WF w PMHx of T2DM, Charcot arthropathy, presents with 
flare of R charcot arthropathy
1. Acute renal failure - Initially thought likely ___ lasix use 
and dehydration as pt reported she was not eating well before 
admission as she felt unwell. her Urine was positive for eos and 
she recently finished a course of augmentin/clindamycin  and 
drug-related renal toxicity was likely the cause of her ARF. 
Pt's Cr came back to 1.0 at discharge (baseline 0.8)

2. UTI - Initially it was unclear as to the reason for her 
leukocytosis and low grade fever & chills, blood cx and cxr were 
neg. Even though she did not have symptoms concerning of UTI, 
she did have leukocytosis and low grade fever with no other 
explanation other than the urinalysis which was dirty with 1 
epi, 110 WBC, moderate bacteria and + leukoesterase. It was 
decide to tx pt with cipro for a 7 day course. UCx was sent but 
pending at ___. Pt denied any known allergy to cipro. PCP, ___. 
___ working w Dr. ___, emailed and will set 
pt up with ___ appt to discuss anemia and ___ on UCx and 
Creatinine

3. Anemia - chronicity unclear, last CBC in OMR from ___. No 
signs of active bleeding, and H/H remained stable.  Iron panel 
was inconclusive. Eventhough she did not have macrocytosis, she 
was noted to have B12 deficiency. Plan was to start her on B12 
supplements but pt refused this. She reports she will discuss 
this with her primary care doctor. 

4. Charcot arthropathy - No fractures or concerns per podiatry. 
Per podiatry, pt can be discharged home from their standpoint, 
with instructions to be non-wt bearing on both feet. There was 
extensive discussion ___ ___, RN, Podiatry team regarding dispo 
issues as pt lived in handicap non-accessible apartment, she 
would need to climb 5 stairs to get inside. Per pt, she cannot 
use wheelchair at home as her apt is small and has thresholds 
between every room. She was offered by ___ to show her show to 
climb the stairs to her apt in a CAM walker, which she initially 
refused and then agreed to. We were not able to arrange 
ambulance ride home given insurance barriers. Pt insisted on 
leaving home and arrangements were made to have her wheeled 
down, so that she can take a cab home, get into appt and her 
friends would help her so that she remained non-wt bearing as 
much as possible. She has a followup appt on ___ with podiatry 
and activity restrictions can be readdressed at that time. Pt 
was also set up by ___ to have home ___ eval.  The issue of DVT 
prophylaxis was discussed with podiatry.  Since lovenox would 
have been difficult to have approved over the weekend and the 
hope is that her non-wt bearing restrictions will be only for a 
few days, podiatry felt comfortable with not discharging pt on 
chemical DVT prophylaxis. Pt was told to do calf exercises, 
watch out for signs/symptoms of DVT and readdress this issue if 
her podiatrist decides that she will be on prolonged immobility. 
Pt was given 20 pills of percocet for pain and told to not 
drive/operate heavy machinary on it. 
5. T2DM - Pt was continued on NPH and humalog SSI
6. Hyperlipidemia - cont simvastatin
7. BLE swelling - per pt, this is chronic and told that in part

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital w Right foot pain, low grade 
temp. You were found to have a UtI and flare of your Charcot 
arthropathy on R foot. You were seen by podiatry who recommended 
CAM walkers, for which you were fitted and they recommended 
non-wt bearing on both feet as much as possible and using 
crutches/cam walker as much as possible. 
You have been started on antibiotics for your urinary tract 
infection, please finish the course.
You were also noted to be anemic and your B12 levels were low. 
You refused to start B12 supplementation now, please follow up 
with your PCP and discuss this with her.
Your kidney function was up on admission, that is likely from 
your recent antibiotic use. The new antibiotic you have been 
placed on for UTI is not similar to that, please have your 
primary care follow up on this. 
Please return to ED for fevers, chills, back pain, worsening 
swelling, pain or redness in feet.
